listings.name: Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: A state pension of $150 a month for veterans who lost, or lost the use of, two or more arms, hands, legs or feet from a service-connected injury or disease.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident when entering the military; Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge; service-connected loss or loss of use of two or more extremities, with a VA compensation rating of 40% or higher in each limb.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in your county. Bring your last DD-214, proof of Pennsylvania residency when you entered the military, and your VA decision letter.
listings.source_title: Amputee and Paralyzed Veterans Pension
listings.notes: New state benefit regulations and revised application forms were issued Oct 24, 2026 (eligibility wording, income limits, cost-of-living allowances); the program page may not reflect them yet, so confirm current rules with the county director. Fillable Oct 2026 forms are on DMVA's Apply for State Veterans' Benefits page (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pennsylvania-veterans/pa-vetconnect/apply-for-state-veterans--benefits); print, sign and deliver them to the county office. DMVA expects an online application system in Nov or Dec 2026. Bills to raise the pension (HB1144, SB534) were pending in the Senate per DMVA materials. Questions: RA-MVVeteransPension@pa.gov.

listings.name: Blind Veterans Pension
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: A state pension of $150 a month for veterans who lost their sight from a service-connected injury or disease.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident when entering the military; Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge; service-connected vision loss with corrected visual acuity of 3/60 or 10/200 (or equivalent) or less in the better eye, or a visual field contracted to 20 degrees or less in the better eye.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in your county. Bring your last DD-214, proof of Pennsylvania residency when you entered the military, and your VA decision letter.
listings.source_title: Blind Veterans Pension
listings.notes: New state benefit regulations and revised application forms were issued Oct 24, 2026 (eligibility wording, income limits, cost-of-living allowances); the program page may not reflect them yet, so confirm current rules with the county director. Fillable Oct 2026 forms are on DMVA's Apply for State Veterans' Benefits page (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pennsylvania-veterans/pa-vetconnect/apply-for-state-veterans--benefits); print, sign and deliver them to the county office. DMVA expects an online application system in Nov or Dec 2026. Questions: RA-MVVeteransPension@pa.gov.

listings.name: Free benefits help from County Directors of Veterans Affairs
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Every Pennsylvania county has a Director of Veterans Affairs who takes applications for state benefits and, with DMVA-accredited Veteran Service Officers, reviews benefits and helps file state and federal claims at no cost.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania veterans, service members, and their families and survivors.
listings.how_to_apply: Find your county director on DMVA's county director page, or find an accredited Veteran Service Officer through PA VetConnect. Bring your DD-214.
listings.source_title: Shapiro Admin Expands Access to Veterans' Benefits Across PA (DMVA, Nov 3, 2026)
listings.notes: Accredited VSO finder: https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pennsylvania-veterans/pa-vetconnect/find-an-accredited-veteran-service-officer. DMVA's release says benefits reviews and application help are free.

listings.name: Delaware Valley Veterans' Home
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: One of Pennsylvania's six state veterans homes run by DMVA. Memory care and skilled nursing care.
listings.eligibility: Veteran who served in the U.S. Armed Forces or Pennsylvania Military Forces and was discharged under honorable conditions, or the spouse or surviving spouse of one. Must be a bona fide Pennsylvania resident with Pennsylvania as home of record at entry into service (current residents get priority). listings.name: Resident Disabled Veteran Hunting and Furtaker Licenses (annual)
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Game Commission
listings.summary: Free annual resident hunting and furtaker licenses for qualifying disabled veterans, plus a disabled veteran antlerless deer license.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident with a service-related disability from a war or armed conflict (WWII Dec 7, 1941-Dec 31, 1946; Korea Jun 27, 1950-Jan 31, 1955; Vietnam era; Persian Gulf Aug 2, 1990-present; Iraq Mar 19, 2003-Dec 15, 2011; Afghanistan Oct 7, 2001-Dec 28, 2014) who has lost one or more limbs, lost the use of one or more limbs, or is certified by the VA as 100% disabled (or receives 100%/total compensation).
listings.how_to_apply: Get the license at a county treasurer or Pennsylvania Game Commission office with your discharge papers and VA disability documentation.
listings.deadline: License year runs July 1 to June 30
listings.cost: Free (lost-license replacement $6.97; one free replacement per year)
listings.source_title: License Types (Pennsylvania Game Commission)
listings.notes: Price of the disabled veteran antlerless deer license was not stated on the page.

listings.name: Resident Disabled Veteran Lifetime Hunting and Furtaker Licenses
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Game Commission
listings.summary: Free lifetime hunting and furtaker licenses for disabled veterans with a permanent qualifying disability; yearly renewals are free.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident with a service-related disability from a war or armed conflict (WWII Dec 7, 1941-Dec 31, 1946; Korea Jun 27, 1950-Jan 31, 1955; Vietnam era; Persian Gulf Aug 2, 1990-present; Iraq Mar 19, 2003-Dec 15, 2011; Afghanistan Oct 7, 2001-Dec 28, 2014) who has lost one or more limbs, lost the use of one or more limbs, or is certified by the VA as 100% disabled (or receives 100%/total compensation). Veterans qualifying by loss of use of a limb or a 100% rating must document that the condition is permanent.
listings.how_to_apply: First lifetime license only at a county treasurer office. Free yearly renewals through HuntFishPA or any issuing agent (first online renewal needs your Social Security number and a PA driver's license or other ID).
listings.deadline: License year runs July 1 to June 30
listings.source_title: License Types (Pennsylvania Game Commission)

listings.name: Disabled Veterans' Real Estate Tax Exemption
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Exempts the home of a qualifying 100% disabled wartime veteran (or unmarried surviving spouse) from real estate taxes.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident; Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge; served during a VA-defined wartime period (an operation or expeditionary medal also counts); VA rating of 100% permanent service-connected, total disability individual unemployability (TDIU), or service-connected blindness, paraplegia or loss of two or more limbs; the home is the principal dwelling, owned solely, jointly with a spouse, or as tenants by the entirety; and financial need. Annual income of $114,637 or less is presumed to show need (effective Jan 1, 2025); above that, need is shown when allowable monthly expenses exceed household income.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live. Veterans previously denied for financial need may reapply under the higher income level.

capacity.served: 28,743 veterans and surviving spouses receiving the exemption, estimated value $98.4 million (as of Sep 24, 2026)
capacity.applicants: 874 applications decided Aug 18 to Sep 24, 2026; 707 approved (81%), 12 denied for financial need, 34 denied for eligibility

odds.text: 707 of 874 applications decided from Aug 18 to Sep 24, 2026 were approved: 81%.

listings.source_title: Real Estate Tax Exemption | Department of Military and Veterans Affairs | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
listings.notes: New state benefit regulations and revised application forms were issued Oct 24, 2026 (eligibility wording, income limits, cost-of-living allowances); the program page may not reflect them yet, so confirm current rules with the county director. Fillable Oct 2026 forms are on DMVA's Apply for State Veterans' Benefits page (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pennsylvania-veterans/pa-vetconnect/apply-for-state-veterans--benefits); print, sign and deliver them to the county office. DMVA expects an online application system in Nov or Dec 2026. A proposed constitutional amendment (HB1257) to change this exemption was pending in the Senate per DMVA meeting materials. Questions: Ra-retx@pa.gov.

listings.name: Educational Gratuity Program
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Pays up to $500 per term or semester, sent directly to the school, for up to eight terms (four school years) for children of veterans who are 100% permanently and totally disabled from service or who died in service during a war or armed conflict.
listings.eligibility: Parent died in service during a period of war or armed conflict, or is a veteran with an Honorable or Under Honorable Conditions discharge who served during VA-defined wartime (or holds an Armed Forces, Navy or Marine Corps Expeditionary Medal) and has a 100% permanent and total service-connected VA rating. Child must be 16 to 23, have lived in Pennsylvania for the five years before applying, attend an approved Pennsylvania school, and show financial need.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in your county. Bring the veteran's last DD-214 or military death certificate, the student's birth certificate, photo ID, and proof of five years of Pennsylvania residency. The school must send proof of enrollment.

Fillable Oct 2026 forms are on DMVA's Apply for State Veterans' Benefits page (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pennsylvania-veterans/pa-vetconnect/apply-for-state-veterans--benefits); print, sign and deliver them to the county office. listings.name: Free vehicle registration for eligible veterans
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT)
listings.summary: Registration and title fees are waived on one passenger vehicle or truck of 9,000 pounds or less for veterans who lost a limb or eye or became partially paralyzed in service, former POWs, Medal of Honor recipients and Purple Heart recipients.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who lost a limb or an eye or became partially paralyzed while serving in the U.S. Armed Forces; former members captured by the enemy in an armed conflict with a DoD campaign medal; Medal of Honor recipients; Purple Heart recipients. Full criteria are on form MV-371DV.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete form MV-371DV with the documents it lists and send it to PennDOT as the form directs.
listings.cost: Free registration and title; license plate fees still apply

listings.name: Military Commercial Driver's License Testing Waiver
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT)
listings.summary: Lets Pennsylvania service members and recently discharged veterans with military truck experience skip the CDL knowledge and/or skills test.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania residents on active or reserve duty, or recent honorably discharged veterans, with at least two years of experience operating a commercial motor vehicle as part of a military job.
listings.how_to_apply: Send forms DL-31CD and DL-11CD with the fee to PennDOT. After you receive the Knowledge Test Authorization Letter, go to a Driver License Center and request the waiver on form DL-398.
listings.cost: Standard CDL application fee (amount not stated on page)
listings.source_title: Military CDL Waiver | Driver and Vehicle Services | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
listings.notes: The page does not define how recent a discharge must be; PennDOT's CDL waiver fact sheet may say.

listings.name: Military Family Relief Assistance Program (MFRAP)
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Need-based emergency grants of up to $5,000 in a 12-month period that do not have to be repaid, for Pennsylvania service members, recently medically discharged members and their families facing a sudden financial need beyond their control.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania residents serving 30+ consecutive days of active duty (not training) in the armed forces or a reserve component, including the PA National Guard; PA Guard members on 30+ days of state active duty; reserve members in good standing for three years after a qualifying tour; or former members for four years after a medical discharge for a service-incurred disability. Dependent spouses and children can apply, and a spouse, parent, sibling or child can apply to visit a hospitalized service member.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the October 2026 MFRAP application (OVA-BVP-032), then hand it to your county veterans affairs office, mail it to DMVA, Lickdale Veterans' Outreach Center (BVP-MFRAP), 40 Fisher Avenue, Jonestown, PA 17038-8202, or fax it to 717-861-9084, attention MFRAP. Do not email applications.

capacity.served: $1,137,071 in MFRAP grants paid from state fiscal year 2005 through 2026; $6,000 paid in state fiscal year 2026-27 through Sep 24, 2026

listings.source_title: Apply for Military Family Relief Assistance
listings.notes: Eligibility and submission details from the Oct 2026 application form (https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/dmva/documents/veterans/vetconnect/documents/ova-bvp-032%20application%20for%20military%20family%20relief%20assistance%20(oct%202026).pdf); the apply page still links an older 2023 form. DMVA says processing can take as little as 48 hours and approval is not guaranteed. Toll-free 800-547-2838. Questions: ra-pa-mfrap@pa.gov.

listings.name: Resident Military Hunting License
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Game Commission
listings.summary: A $2.97 resident hunting license for Pennsylvanians on full-time active duty.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania resident (home of record) on active full-time duty in the U.S. Armed Forces or Coast Guard who is stationed outside Pennsylvania (with official orders) or home on leave (with leave papers).
listings.how_to_apply: Buy from a license issuing agent with your orders or leave papers.
listings.deadline: License year runs July 1 to June 30
listings.source_title: License Types (Pennsylvania Game Commission)
listings.notes: The page lists this under general hunting licenses without naming where to buy; an armed forces antlerless deer license is also listed without a price.

listings.name: U.S. military and veteran registration plates
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT)
listings.summary: About 40 specialty plates for veterans, current service members, Guard, Gold Star and Blue Star families, campaigns (Korea, Vietnam, Persian Gulf, OEF, OIF, Inherent Resolve) and decorations (Purple Heart, Bronze Star, Silver Star, Combat Infantryman Badge and others). Purple Heart holders get free registration for one vehicle; ex-POW and Medal of Honor plates can be had for a processing fee in place of registration fees.
listings.eligibility: Depends on the plate. Veteran plates need a discharge other than dishonorable (DD-214) or a retiree ID; campaign and award plates need the medal or service shown on the DD-214; current-member plates are self-certified; Gold Star and Blue Star plates are for family members who own or co-own the vehicle.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the form named for your plate (mostly MV-150V for veteran plates, MV-150P, MV-150C, MV-150AD, MV-912 Gold Star, MV-920 Blue Star) with your documents; Medal of Honor requests go through DMVA at Fort Indiantown Gap. Fees are on PennDOT form MV-70S.
listings.cost: Plate and registration fees per PennDOT MV-70S; free registration for one vehicle for Purple Heart; processing fee only for ex-POW and Medal of Honor
listings.source_title: U.S. Military Registration Plates fact sheet (PennDOT, April 2026)
listings.notes: The fact sheet does not cover Disabled Veteran or Severely Disabled Veteran plates, which DMVA's State Veterans Programs page lists separately; those pages were not read.

listings.name: Pennsylvania National Guard Survivor's Pension
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Monthly state pension for the family of a Pennsylvania National Guard member killed in the line of duty on state active duty: $100 to $300 a month for a surviving spouse depending on children, payments for minor children if there is no spouse, or $100 for dependent parents.
listings.eligibility: Survivors of a PA Army or Air National Guard member who was killed or died of line-of-duty injuries on state active duty under the Governor's orders (including armory assemblies and training flights). Not for deaths in federal service, in war or under the President's orders. Spouse is paid up to 10 years or until remarriage; dependent parents up to 10 years; minor children until 18.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the October 2026 application (OVA-BVP-013) and submit it through your county veterans affairs office, by mail to DMVA, Lickdale Veterans' Outreach Center (BVP-Pensions), 40 Fisher Avenue, Jonestown, PA 17038-8202, or by fax to 717-861-9084, attention Pensions. Include ID, marriage or birth certificates, the death certificate and the line-of-duty determination.
listings.source_title: Application for Pennsylvania National Guard Survivor's Pension (OVA-BVP Form 013, Rev. Oct 2026)

listings.name: Tuition Waiver for Pennsylvania National Guard Survivors
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Tuition and fee waiver at Pennsylvania state-owned and state-related universities, community colleges and technical schools for the spouse and children of a Pennsylvania National Guard member who died in the line of duty.
listings.eligibility: Spouse or child of a PA Army or Air National Guard member who was a Pennsylvania resident and was killed, or died of injuries, in the line of duty on federal or state active duty. The survivor must be a Pennsylvania resident eligible for in-state tuition. A spouse can use it for up to ten years after the death or until remarriage.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the October 2026 application (OVA-BVP-023) and submit it through your county veterans affairs office, by mail to DMVA, Lickdale Veterans' Outreach Center (BVP-TWP), 40 Fisher Avenue, Jonestown, PA 17038-8202, or by fax to 717-861-9084, attention TWP. Include ID, marriage or birth certificate, the death certificate and the line-of-duty determination.
listings.location: Participating Pennsylvania public universities, community colleges and technical schools
listings.source_title: Tuition Waiver Application for Pennsylvania National Guard Survivors (OVA-BVP Form 023, Rev. Oct 2026)
listings.notes: The form lists approved schools by code on page 2; it does not state an age limit for children.

listings.how_to_apply: Use DMVA's Apply for Veterans' Home Residency page. Admission is first-come, first-served and the home's admissions committee sets the level of care.
listings.location: Near downtown Pittsburgh, Allegheny County, PA
listings.cost: Monthly payment toward the maintenance fee based on ability to pay (no dollar amounts published)

capacity.waitlist: 16 on the nursing care waitlist, veterans and spouses (Sep 16, 2026)

listings.source_title: Pennsylvania Veterans Homes | Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Bed, census and waitlist figures come from DMVA's Oct 2, 2026 State Veterans' Commission read-ahead (census taken Sep 16, 2026); per-home waitlist numbers were read from that table and include spouses. Statewide totals that day: 1,148 nursing care beds, 321 personal care beds, 1,211 residents, waitlists of 124 veterans and 39 spouses (nursing) and 11 veterans and 2 spouses (personal care). Eligibility from https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pa-veterans-homes/eligibility. Homes email: RA-MVVA-Homes@pa.gov.

listings.name: PA VetConnect
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: DMVA's statewide referral network: field staff in all 67 counties connect veterans with state, federal and community resources, including help for veterans facing homelessness.
listings.eligibility: Pennsylvania veterans and their families.
listings.how_to_apply: Start on DMVA's PA VetConnect page or email RA-MVVet-Connect@pa.gov; your County Director of Veterans Affairs can also refer you.
listings.source_title: Homeless Veterans | Department of Military and Veterans Affairs | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
listings.notes: DMVA states that programs specifically for homeless veterans are not funded through its budget; it links veterans to VTA, MFRAP, VA (VISN 4, SSVF, HUD-VASH) and the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (877-424-3838).

listings.name: Veterans designation on driver's license or ID card
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT)
listings.summary: A free 'Veteran' designation on your Pennsylvania driver's license or photo ID, handy for proving veteran status for discounts and services; it carries over at every renewal.
listings.eligibility: Anyone with a DD-214 or equivalent showing U.S. Armed Forces service (including reserve and National Guard) and discharge under conditions other than dishonorable.
listings.how_to_apply: Add it online through PennDOT's driver's license login (license number, date of birth and last 4 of SSN) or mail form DL-80 to Bureau of Driver Licensing, P.O. Box 68272, Harrisburg, PA 17106-8272. CDL holders mail DL-143CD (renewal) or DL-80CD (duplicate).
listings.cost: No fee for the designation; normal license or ID renewal or duplicate fees apply
listings.source_title: Veterans Designation | Driver and Vehicle Services | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania

listings.name: Volunteer at Pennsylvania's state veterans homes
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: The six DMVA veterans homes rely on community volunteers; DMVA reports 2,993 volunteers donating 100,000 hours.
listings.eligibility: Members of the public, including veterans; the homes page does not list volunteer requirements.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact DMVA's Bureau of Veterans Homes (800-547-2838, RA-MVVA-Homes@pa.gov) or the home nearest you through the request-information page.
listings.location: Philadelphia, Scranton, Duncansville, Erie, Spring City and Pittsburgh areas, PA

capacity.served: 2,993 volunteers donated 100,000 hours (period not stated on page)

listings.source_title: Pennsylvania Veterans Homes | Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: The volunteer figures appear on the homes page without a time period. The page read does not describe a volunteer application process.

listings.name: Pennsylvania Veterans Registry
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Free DMVA sign-up that sends veterans and families information on state programs and services, including the monthly 'Together We Serve' newsletter and breaking news.
listings.eligibility: Open to veterans, their family members and anyone who works with veterans; you do not need to be a veteran.
listings.how_to_apply: Subscribe online through DMVA's Veterans Registry form.
listings.source_title: Subscribe to Veterans' Registry and Monthly Publication

listings.name: Veterans Temporary Assistance (VTA)
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: Temporary financial help of up to $1,600 in a 12-month period for the necessities of life: food, shelter, fuel and clothing.
listings.eligibility: Bona fide Pennsylvania resident who is a veteran discharged under honorable conditions after active duty (not active duty for training), a veteran with a VA-certified service-connected disability, or the unmarried surviving spouse of an eligible veteran (including one who died in service). Must have a temporary shortfall caused by something beyond your control (illness, disability, unemployment, disaster) and not enough aid from other state or federal programs. Receiving food stamps does not disqualify you.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the County Director of Veterans Affairs in the county where you live. Bring your DD-214, proof of Pennsylvania residency, proof of income and expenses, and current mortgage, rent and utility receipts.

capacity.served: 112 VTA grants paid in state fiscal year 2026-27 through Sep 24, 2026 ($172,880)

listings.source_title: Veterans Temporary Assistance | Department of Military and Veterans Affairs | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
listings.notes: New state benefit regulations and revised application forms were issued Oct 24, 2026 (eligibility wording, income limits, cost-of-living allowances); the program page may not reflect them yet, so confirm current rules with the county director. Fillable Oct 2026 forms are on DMVA's Apply for State Veterans' Benefits page (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dmva/pennsylvania-veterans/pa-vetconnect/apply-for-state-veterans--benefits); print, sign and deliver them to the county office. DMVA expects an online application system in Nov or Dec 2026. Program questions: RA-VTA@pa.gov (no applications by email).

listings.name: Veterans' Trust Fund Grant Program
listings.organization: Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs (DMVA)
listings.summary: State grants to nonprofits, veterans service organizations and counties that serve Pennsylvania veterans; this cycle's priorities are mental and behavioral health, transportation and employment for organizations, and expanded programming and direct services for counties.
listings.eligibility: 501(c)(19) veterans service organizations and 501(c)(3) nonprofits whose mission serves Pennsylvania veterans (up to $40,000), and Pennsylvania counties individually or jointly or the PA Association of County Directors of Veterans Affairs (up to $15,000 per county). Not for individual veterans; individuals in need use Veterans Temporary Assistance, which the Trust Fund also pays for.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online only through PA eGrants at grants.pa.gov with a Keystone login; paper applications are not considered. Read the FY27 Request for Applications and applicant instructions linked on the DMVA page first.
listings.deadline: Grant cycle open Nov 2, 2026; applications due by 2 p.m. Eastern, Dec 18, 2026
listings.source_title: Veterans' Trust Fund | Department of Military and Veterans Affairs | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
listings.notes: For organizations and counties, not individuals. The page calls this the 2027-28 cycle while the linked RFA is labeled FY27. Grant agreements take about two months after award. Questions: RA-MVVetTrustFund@pa.gov.
